key_insight: DFT-trained machine-learning surrogates enable efficient sampling of small-polaron hopping and quantitative conductivity prediction in defected Li₄Ti₅O₁₂ (LTO).
engineering_relevance: The workflow reduces the computational cost of modeling charge transport in a battery anode material under realistic defect conditions.
method: Calculate small-polaron configurations and hopping barriers using DFT.
Train ML surrogates to estimate barriers across symmetry-inequivalent hopping pathways.
Feed surrogate predictions into a kinetic model to estimate conductivity.
evidence_signal: Using 154 barrier calculations out of 3,649 symmetry-inequivalent cases, the workflow achieved over 20-fold computational efficiency and predicted room-temperature conductivity of 6.7 × 10⁻³ S/cm, within the experimental range.
watch_item: Validation beyond LTO remains necessary; accuracy may depend on whether DFT training data cover the relevant defect environments and hopping pathways.
paper_title: A Machine-learning-aided Workflow for Sampling Small Polaron Dynamics in Energy Materials
